review_type: Repository-owner-commissioned AI-assisted Econometrica numerical-methods advisory review
recommendation: Reject in the present form and do not invite another ordinary revision of the cumulative manuscript. A new, sharply focused paper on owner-preserving compilation and resource-certified policy construction for constrained Lipschitz dynamic programs could merit evaluation, but R49 does not establish an Econometrica-level method-specific advantage for Neural Bellman Operators.

main_study.push_status: The workflow locally committed 842 evidence files, but the GitHub push failed with an HTTP 500; the immutable artifact was preserved.

blocking_findings: R49 is not a canonical, self-contained submitted manuscript: there is no R49 review-ready branch, response, generated table directory, committed main evidence archive, release audit or compiled R49 publication.
The owner-preserving compiler is a method-neutral min-plus/Lipschitz-envelope algorithm; its ReLU encoding does not identify a neural computational advantage.
Actual policy costs favor tensor FVI in 93 of 96 R49 comparisons, are unresolved in three, and never favor witness; all 64 target-one and target-two comparisons favor FVI.
Certificate attainment and actual policy quality point in opposite directions, so a work-to-certificate frontier is not an economic performance frontier.
The original curvature-FVI baseline produces zero nonuniform date models; all 72 matched checkpoints are substantively identical to uniform FVI and add about 15 percent median overhead.
The prospective graded-FVI baseline is genuinely nonuniform but has a worse final bound and higher complete-prefix time in all twelve matched services.
The dimension study remains a low-dimensional tensor-cover stress test through dimension four and does not establish a common-accuracy scaling law.
The separated-resource allocation theorem optimizes a Bellman-query proxy and is not prospectively executed as a complete adaptive algorithm.
The priced-sensor catalogue is economically underidentified: 101 of 104 contrasts are unresolved and the bit prices are uncalibrated normalized primitives.
The cumulative platform scope and economic claims remain disproportionate to the narrow compiled-witness and normalized-investment evidence established by R49.
positive_findings: The original-owner multidimensional distance-transform theorem is a useful policy-preserving compilation result.
State, action and innovation error resources are separated explicitly.
R49 compares actual first-crossing policy costs rather than subtracting regret bounds.
Dimension-three and dimension-four stress runs exercise the compilation mechanism.
The adaptive-baseline defect is identified before graded outcomes are inspected, and the original block is preserved.
The complete frozen tolerance frontier and adverse direct-cost signs are retained.
Artifact provenance, result hashing, failure preservation and auditability remain unusually strong.

limitations: The reviewer did not rerun construction, scientific simulation, LaTeX or timing services; new executions would create new observations.

The audit verifies every frozen result bundled in the artifacts and all bundled source hashes; inherited source files omitted from the artifacts are identified rather than silently claimed as reverified.
The theorem chain was spot-checked for internal consistency but this report is not an independent proof of every inherited theorem.
Single-runner clocks are descriptive and support no hardware-general performance inference.
No claim is made that tensor or graded FVI dominates outside the declared R49 economies.
This advisory review is not an Econometric Society editorial decision.
